transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, mostly it’s this memorial for my brother. I started out just wanting to do something nice, you know, a few songs, maybe some photos, but it’s gotten… bigger. I’m spending most days calling people, tracking down music, planning displays, even thinking about trips connected to it.

My wife says I’ve let the garden go, and I haven’t been keeping up with my walking group either. She says I’ve pushed just about everything else aside. I don’t know, it feels important, but I guess it’s gotten away from me some.
Have you noticed your energy levels or mood being unusually high or elevated while working on these memorial plans, like you don’t need much sleep or feel like you can take on more than usual?

Yeah… I suppose I do get kind of lit up by it. Like I’ll be sitting there with the old photos and the songs, and suddenly it feels like there’s a real purpose to it, like the whole town is finally going to understand what our family was about.

But then if my wife says, “Maybe that’s too much,” or someone at the senior center wants to change where a display goes, I get sharp with them. I don’t mean to, but I snap because it feels like they’re slowing down something important.
Have you noticed that you’ve needed less sleep lately while working on the memorial plans?

I’m not really sure about the sleep part. I mean, I stay up sometimes looking through things, but I haven’t kept track of whether it’s less sleep exactly. My wife would probably know better than me—she notices everything, like when I leave papers all over the dining table. We used to keep that table clear for Sunday dinners, back when my brother would come over… but no, I don’t know if I’d say I’ve needed less sleep.
Have you found yourself spending much more time on this memorial project than you originally intended, to the point where it feels like it’s taking over your daily routine?

Yes… yes, I think that’s fair. It started as just a little memorial for my brother—some songs, a few pictures, nothing too fancy. But now I’m spending most days on it, calling people, chasing down old music, figuring out displays, even thinking about trips tied to it.

My wife says I’ve let the garden go, and I haven’t been going with my walking group like I used to. The garden, you know, my brother always liked the tomatoes we grew out there—anyway, yes, it’s taken over more than I meant it to. I guess I keep finding one more thing that has to be done.
Have you found yourself spending more money than you originally planned or making big decisions without thinking them through as part of organizing the memorial?

I don’t know that I’d call it big decisions, exactly. I mean, I’ve bought some things here and there for it, but I haven’t really sat down and added it all up. My wife handles more of that kind of keeping-track than I do.

There was this one old frame I saw that reminded me of something my mother had in the hallway years ago—funny how a frame can bring a whole house back to you, the wallpaper and everything. But as far as spending more than planned… I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that, no.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your garden or walking group, while focusing on this memorial?

Yes… I suppose I have. I used to be regular with the walking group, and book club too, but I’ve missed those. And the garden’s gotten away from me—there are weeds where I used to keep it neat.

It’s not that I don’t care about those things. It’s just the memorial display keeps pulling me back in. I’ll think of one more person to call, or one more thing that has to be right. My wife says our whole day ends up being about either calming me down or steering me away from another phone call or trip or argument about it.

And I think I’ve upset some people at the senior center because I keep turning every conversation back to the display. I don’t mean to. It just feels… important, and then suddenly that’s all I’m talking about.
Have you had any distinct periods where your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable—like you were on a roll with the memorial plans and nothing could slow you down?

Yes… there are times it feels like I’m lit up, like I’ve got this purpose and everything is finally lining up. Like if I can just get the display right, the whole town will understand what my family was, what my brother meant.

And then if my wife says, “Maybe slow down,” or someone at the senior center questions where something should go, I can snap. I don’t always mean to, but it’s like they’re standing in the doorway when I’m trying to carry something important through. My wife says I get that tone… and I suppose I do. I get wound up, and then suddenly I’m angry that people aren’t keeping up.
Have there been times when your mood was so unusually high, excited, or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, lasting for several days in a row?

Yes… yes, I think so. It can go on for days where I’m just—well, “up” isn’t quite the word, but lit up, like there’s a current running through me and the memorial is the thing I was meant to get right.

I’ll be thinking, the whole town is finally going to understand our family, you know? My brother, my mother, all of it. And then if my wife says maybe I should leave it for tomorrow, or someone at the senior center questions where something should be placed, I can get sharp. I snap. I don’t like that I do, but in that moment it feels like they’re slowing down something important.
Have there been times when your mood was so unusually high, excited, or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, and this lasted for at least a week straight?

Yes… I’d say it has. Maybe a week, yes. My wife would probably say longer, but I lose track when I’m in it.

I’ll feel lit up, like I’ve got this purpose and the whole town is finally going to understand our family if I get the display just right. And then—well, like last time at the senior center, someone asked whether one of the photos really belonged there, and I got sharp. I could hear myself snapping, same way I do with my wife when she tells me to slow down.

It’s not my usual self, no. I’m usually more… even, I think. But when this takes hold, I feel driven, and if anyone questions it, I get irritable fast.
